label: History
value: Anne Shirley was born in Bolingbroke, Nova Scotia.
unit: Born in Bolingbroke, Nova Scotia, Anne Shirley was an orphan who lived with Mrs. Thomas, Mrs. Hammond, and in an asylum before arriving at Green Gables fourteen years prior to her marriage. Though Marilla Cuthbert initially intended to send her back because they had expected a boy, Marilla eventually agreed to keep and raise her. Anne formed a deep bond with Diana Barry, created the Avonlea Village Improvement Society, and pursued higher education at Queen's Academy and Redmond College. Despite rejecting early proposals from classmates, she eventually accepted Gilbert Blythe, and the couple married and relocated to Four Winds Harbor. In their new home, Anne became close friends with her tragic neighbor Leslie Moore and the elderly lighthouse keeper Captain Jim. After suffering the loss of her firstborn daughter, Joyce, Anne later gave birth to a healthy son named James Matthew. Following Captain Jim's peaceful death, Anne and Gilbert prepared to leave their initial home of dreams to move into a larger house in the Glen.

label: Quote
value: Anne Shirley said: "Pretty well. I imagine a good deal, and that helps to pass the time. Of course, it’s rather lonesome. But then, I may as well get used to that."

label: Quote
value: Anne Shirley said: "I don’t get cross about other things; but I’m so tired of being twitted about my hair and it just makes me boil right over. Do you suppose my hair will really be a handsome auburn when I grow up?"

label: Quote
value: Anne Shirley said: "I love pretty things; and I hate to look in the glass and see something that isn’t pretty. It makes me feel so sorrowful—just as I feel when I look at any ugly thing. I pity it because it isn’t beautiful."

label: Quote
value: Anne Shirley said: "I love Green Gables already, and I never loved any place before. No place ever seemed like home. Oh, Marilla, I’m so happy. I could pray right now and not find it a bit hard."

label: Quote
value: Anne Shirley said: "Oh, Marilla, I’m frightened—now that it has come I’m actually frightened. What if she shouldn’t like me! It would be the most tragical disappointment of my life."

label: Diana Barry
value: Diana is Anne's sworn bosom friend.
unit: Diana is Anne's sworn bosom friend and constant companion, with whom she plays, attends school, and rows on the pond [R2, R3, S2, S3]. label: Gilbert Blythe
value: Anne and Gilbert have a bitter childhood enmity.
unit: Anne and Gilbert's relationship evolves from a bitter childhood enmity into a loving marriage [R7, R10]. Their initial grudge begins when Gilbert pulls Anne's braid and calls her 'Carrots,' leading Anne to smash a slate over his head and refuse his apology [S8]. Though they remain fierce academic rivals throughout their school years, Anne secretly forgives him and later refuses his rescue offer after being stranded on a bridge pile [R4, S11, S12]. Over time, their hostility softens into literary collaboration and close friendship before Gilbert's long-held romantic feelings culminate in their marriage by Volume 4 [R5, R8, R9, R10].

label: History
value: Aunt Jamesina was named after James.
unit: Aunt Jamesina was named after her father, James, who drowned at sea shortly before her birth, and she grew up wishing for a yellow silk dress that neither her mother nor her husband permitted her to have. Known for teasing her suitors in her youth, she taught her daughter to cook before college and prayed for her to become a missionary. Later in life, she moved into Patty's Place alongside her cats, Joseph and the Sarah-cat, to chaperon Anne Shirley and her friends during their college years. Over the course of their time together, she managed the household, shared her pragmatic yet humorous views on life and love, and offered a grounding presence through the girls' academic studies, social gatherings, and romantic entanglements. At the end of their four years of college, she reflected with the household on the enduring value of common sense and life lessons before the group dissolved Patty's Place upon graduation.

label: Quote
value: Aunt Jamesina said: "Kittens have to be drowned, I admit, or the world would be overrun. But no decent, grown-up cat should be done to death—unless he sucks eggs."

label: Quote
value: Aunt Jamesina said: "Well, I hope so, Anne. I do hope so, because I love her. But I can’t understand her—she beats me. She isn’t like any of the girls I ever knew, or any of the girls I was myself."

label: Quote
value: Aunt Jamesina said: "Yes, in my soul. But I’ll admit my legs aren’t as young as yours. You go and get some fresh air, Anne. You look pale lately."

label: Quote
value: Aunt Jamesina said: "Anybody is liable to rheumatism in her legs, Anne. It’s only old people who should have rheumatism in their souls, though. Thank goodness, I never have. When you get rheumatism in your soul you might as well go and pick out your coffin."

label: Quote
value: Aunt Jamesina said: "I’ve got them yet. There are three old widowers at home who have been casting sheep’s eyes at me for some time. You children needn’t think you own all the romance in the world."

label: History
value: Charlotta the Fourth worked as a young helper for Miss Lavendar Lewis at Echo Lodge.
unit: Charlotta the Fourth worked as a young helper and maid for Miss Lavendar Lewis at Echo Lodge, where she assisted with household duties, picked strawberries, and expressed deep concern when her employer was feeling unusually despondent. Following the resolution of Miss Lavendar's romance, Charlotta excitedly prepared for a move to Boston and helped tidy Echo Lodge after Miss Lavendar's garden wedding. Years later, she returned to Green Gables as one of the guests attending Anne's wedding, and she eventually married a good-tempered American bricklayer named Tom.

label: History
value: Cornelia Bryant was an only child for eight years.
unit: Miss Cornelia Bryant was an only child for eight years before her younger brother was born, and she later raised him after their mother died until he passed away in his twenties. In her youth, she could have chosen among many suitors—including Amos Grant—and won first prize for lemon pies ten years prior. Residing at Four Winds Harbor, she frequently visited Anne Shirley and Gilbert Blythe to sew, drop off news, and express her sharp opinions on religion, townspeople, and men. She formed a close connection with the Blythe household, joining them for holidays and offering support through tragic events, such as the loss of Anne's newborn daughter Joyce and the birth of baby James Matthew. Miss Cornelia also shared the tragic history of her friend Leslie Moore with Anne, and she initially reacted with anger when Gilbert proposed a medical operation in Montreal for Leslie's husband, Dick. However, she was left utterly shocked upon learning that the man was actually Dick's lookalike cousin George, freeing Leslie from her marriage, after which Miss Cornelia urged Anne to notify Leslie's suitor Owen Ford. She eventually stunned her friends by announcing her own upcoming marriage to Marshall Elliott, detailing her wedding plans and lightheartedly exchanging banter with Gilbert about managing a husband.

Residing at Four Winds Harbor, she frequently visited Anne Shirley and Gilbert Blythe to sew, drop off news, and express her sharp opinions on religion, townspeople, and men. She formed a close connection with the Blythe household, joining them for holidays and offering support through tragic events, such as the loss of Anne's newborn daughter Joyce and the birth of baby James Matthew. Miss Cornelia also shared the tragic history of her friend Leslie Moore with Anne, and she initially reacted with anger when Gilbert proposed a medical operation in Montreal for Leslie's husband, Dick. However, she was left utterly shocked upon learning that the man was actually Dick's lookalike cousin George, freeing Leslie from her marriage, after which Miss Cornelia urged Anne to notify Leslie's suitor Owen Ford. She eventually stunned her friends by announcing her own upcoming marriage to Marshall Elliott, detailing her wedding plans and lightheartedly exchanging banter with Gilbert about managing a husband.

label: Quote
value: Cornelia Bryant said: "You always look as cool as a cucumber, Anne, dearie. Do I smell cherry pie? If I do, ask me to stay to tea. Haven’t tasted a cherry pie this summer. My cherries have all been stolen by those scamps of Gilman boys from the Glen."

label: History
value: Davy Keith lost his father as an infant.
unit: Davy Keith lost his father as an infant and was raised without proper guidance, developing a reputation as a holy terror for mischief before arriving at Green Gables with his twin sister Dora. Shortly after his arrival, Davy locked Dora in a toolhouse, but he tearfully promised never to lie again after realizing he had made Anne Shirley cry. Despite his persistent troublemaking—such as stealing jam and accidentally ruining lemon pies meant for a guest—Marilla Cuthbert and Anne developed a fond affection for him. Davy's permanent stay at Green Gables was secured when word arrived that Richard Keith had died and left money in trust for the twins. Over time, Davy looked to Anne for comfort and guidance, expressing a deep fondness for her, confessing his jealousies, and admitting his struggles with bad language and guilty conscience when he broke rules. Later in his youth, he convinced Dora to skip Sunday School to go fishing, but he ultimately confessed his misdeeds and lies to Anne. Though Davy continued his lively antics, he showed significant growth in behavior and maturity as he grew older.

Despite his persistent troublemaking—such as stealing jam and accidentally ruining lemon pies meant for a guest—Marilla Cuthbert and Anne developed a fond affection for him. Davy's permanent stay at Green Gables was secured when word arrived that Richard Keith had died and left money in trust for the twins. Over time, Davy looked to Anne for comfort and guidance, expressing a deep fondness for her, confessing his jealousies, and admitting his struggles with bad language and guilty conscience when he broke rules. Later in his youth, he convinced Dora to skip Sunday School to go fishing, but he ultimately confessed his misdeeds and lies to Anne. Though Davy continued his lively antics, he showed significant growth in behavior and maturity as he grew older.

value: Davy Keith said: "I just did it for fun. Things have been so awful quiet here for so long that I thought it would be fun to give you folks a big scare. It was, too."

label: Quote
value: Davy Keith said: “I never will, now that I know it’s bad,” asseverated Davy between sobs. “If you ever catch me telling a whopper again you can . . .” Davy groped mentally for a suitable penance . . . “you can skin me alive, Anne.”

label: Quote
value: Davy Keith said: “Why?” queried Davy, settling comfortably down and looking up with a tearstained, investigating face. “Why ain’t whopper as good as falsehood? I want to know. It’s just as big a word.”

label: Quote
value: Davy Keith said: “Then,” said Davy decidedly, “Marilla is bad, for she tells them. And she’s worse’n me, for I didn’t know it was wrong but she does.”

label: Quote
value: Davy Keith said: “But I tell you there is,” persisted Davy. “It was in that question Marilla taught me last Sunday. ‘Why should we love God?’ It says, ‘Because He makes preserves, and redeems us.’ Preserves is just a holy way of saying jam.”

label: History
value: Diana Barry was named by a schoolmaster.
unit: Diana Barry was named by a schoolmaster who was boarding with her family when she was born. During her youth, she met Anne Shirley at Orchard Slope, where they pledged eternal friendship, and they frequently signaled to each other across distance using candle flashes. The girls attended school together, where Diana welcomed Anne back after Anne was temporarily forbidden to play with her and when Anne refused to attend school following a punishment. Diana also accompanied Anne on local outings, such as canvassing for the Village Improvement Society, searching for a willow-ware platter at Spencervale, and discovering Miss Lavendar Lewis at Echo Lodge. Over the years, Diana served as a trusted confidante for Anne's creative pursuits, including the creation of a story club in their youth and reviewing Anne's written story, Averil's Atonement. As they grew older, Diana became engaged to Fred Wright, and Anne served as a helper when Diana married Fred at Orchard Slope. Four years after her marriage, Diana gave birth to a baby boy.

value: Dick Moore inherited a sea-going streak from his mother.
unit: Dick Moore inherited a sea-going streak from his mother and divided his time between sailing in the summer, working in his father's store in the winter, and owning a dog named Carlo. He settled with Leslie on the West place for a winter, but he was a drunkard who went to Nova Scotia to visit relatives before dying of yellow fever in Cuba thirteen years prior. A letter eventually revealed that the man long believed to be Dick was actually his lookalike cousin, George Moore.

She approaches activities, such as gardening, in a careful, systematic, and industrious manner, maintaining a composed and placid demeanor even under pressure. As she grows, she proves to be remarkably sensible, womanly, and helpful, though her prim and predictable nature can make her seem somewhat monotonous.

label: History
value: Dora Keith moved to Green Gables.
unit: Dora Keith moved to Green Gables alongside her twin brother, Davy, though she was noted for her quiet perfection compared to her brother's unruly nature. Shortly after her arrival, Davy caused her to fall into a pigpen and later locked her in a toolhouse, prompting a frantic search by the household before she was found. Following the death of Richard Keith, money was left in trust for Dora and her brother, allowing them to remain permanently at Green Gables. She later attended school, where she was once frightened by a classmate's ghost stories, and was eventually persuaded by Davy to skip Sunday School to go fishing.

label: History
value: Gilbert Blythe returned to Avonlea
unit: Gilbert Blythe returned to Avonlea after spending three years in Alberta with his sick father and a summer visiting cousins. Upon his return to school, he pulled Anne Shirley's braid and called her 'Carrots,' prompting her to smash a slate over his head and refuse his apology. Their fierce academic rivalry continued through their school years, though Gilbert eventually saved Anne from a leaking boat on the pond and offered his friendship, which she angrily rejected. After completing his studies at Queen's Academy and winning the medal, Gilbert gave up his appointment at the Avonlea school so Anne could take it, leading them to finally end their feud and become close friends. Gilbert then attended Redmond College, where he led his freshman class to victory in the Arts Rush and co-founded the Avonlea Village Improvement Society during his breaks. During their time at college, Gilbert confessed his love and proposed to Anne, but she rejected him, breaking his heart and severing their close friendship. After recovering from a life-threatening bout of typhoid fever, he proposed to her a second time in Hester Gray's garden, and she happily accepted. Following their wedding, Gilbert carried Anne into their new house at Four Winds Harbor, where he established his medical practice. When he realized that their neighbor Dick Moore's memory could be restored through surgery, he dutifully informed Leslie Moore despite Anne's objections, a choice that ultimately revealed Dick was actually his cousin George. Following the loss of their firstborn infant, Joyce, Gilbert and Anne welcomed a healthy baby boy named James Matthew. Gilbert eventually proposed buying the Morgan place in the Glen, leading the couple to move into their new home after saying goodbye to their house of dreams.

label: Personality
value: Harrison is fussy.
unit: Harrison is a fussy, fidgety, and middle-aged man who has earned a reputation for being an odd crank. Though he prides himself on his outspokenness, which others can find trying, he maintains an outwardly sympathetic and kind nature. He routinely smokes a pipe on his veranda and holds a prejudice against marriage, though he is later described as a changed and much nicer man after remarrying. He is also fastidious and hard to please when reviewing written work.

label: History
value: Before settling in Avonlea, Harrison lived in Scottsford, New Brunswick.
unit: Before settling in Avonlea, Harrison lived in Scottsford, New Brunswick, having visited Prince Edward Island as a boy. Following a promise made to his dying sister, he married Emily Scott and took a fortnight's wedding trip to St. John, though he later kept a bachelor's hall after his sister passed away. Upon moving to Avonlea as Anne Shirley's neighbor, he initially confronted her angrily when a cow broke into his oatfield, but the two formed an unexpected friendship after Anne accidentally sold his Jersey cow and came to his house with a cake and money to confess. Over time, Harrison offered his opinions on Anne's teaching methods, discussed village news, and survived a severe storm that tragically killed his parrot, Ginger. Eventually, Harrison explained the history of his marriage and past falling out to Anne, leading to his reunion with his wife Emily. Harrison continued to support Anne's endeavors, providing feedback on her story Averil's Atonement, encouraging her to keep writing despite early magazine rejections, and delivering her mail during a stormy winter holiday.

value: Harrison said: "Sorry, miss! Sorry isn’t going to help matters any. You’d better go and look at the havoc that animal has made in my oats . . . trampled them from center to circumference, miss."

label: Quote
value: Harrison said: “Who? Mrs. Lynde? Don’t you tell me I’m like that old gossip,” said Mr. Harrison irritably. “I’m not . . . not a bit. What have you got in that box?”

label: Quote
value: Harrison said: "I don’t, that’s a fact, and I’m mighty fond of it, too. I’m much obliged to you. It looks good on top. I hope it’s good all the way through."

label: Quote
value: Harrison said: "Well, I’ll tell you what, miss, you must help me eat it. I’ll put the kettle on and we’ll have a cup of tea. How will that do?"

label: Quote
value: Harrison said: "I see you haven’t much confidence in my ability to make tea. You’re wrong . . . I can brew up as good a jorum of tea as you ever drank. But go ahead yourself. Fortunately it rained last Sunday, so there’s plenty of clean dishes."

label: History
value: Jane Andrews was a schoolgirl in Avonlea.
unit: Jane Andrews was a schoolgirl in Avonlea who belonged to a Story Club alongside Anne, Diana, and Ruby. She later attended a benefit concert at the White Sands Hotel with Anne and Billy Andrews, traveling home together afterward to discuss wealth and contentment. When Anne began teaching, Jane met with her and Gilbert to debate classroom discipline and corporal punishment. She joined her friends to react in dismay when the local hall was mistakenly painted bright blue, spent a spring afternoon picnicking with Anne, Priscilla, and Diana in Hester Gray's garden, and joined a committee with Anne and Diana to unsuccessfully persuade Judson Parker regarding advertisement signs on his fences. Jane eventually taught school on the western prairies after resigning from her position at the Avonlea school. She acted as a proxy to propose to Anne on behalf of her brother Billy, taking Anne's refusal coldly, and later married a millionaire, traveling to Europe for her wedding tour.

label: History
value: Janet Sweet lost her sister Anne when she was young.
unit: Janet Sweet, who lost her sister Anne when she was young, worked as a pleasant landlady at Wayside, where she befriended her boarder Anne. After twenty years of silent courtship from her admirer John Douglas, Janet took Anne's advice to take a firm stand and sharply rejected his escort after a prayer meeting, though Anne quickly rushed to reconcile the pair. Following the eventual death of John's mother, John proposed to Janet, revealing he had been bound by a promise to his mother to wait until after her passing before marrying or telling anyone.

label: Quote
value: Janet said: "If she wasn’t—but she is. So we mustn’t speak evil of her. But I’m happy at last, Anne. And I wouldn’t have minded waiting so long a bit if I’d only known why."

label: Quote
value: Janet said: "Oh, she does. She’s told me time and again that she’d love to see John settled before her time comes. She’s always giving him hints—you heard her yourself the other day. I thought I’d ha’ gone through the floor."

label: Quote
value: Janet said: “I couldn’t,” said poor Janet pathetically. “You see, Anne, I’ve always been awful fond of John. He might just as well keep coming as not, for there was never anybody else I’d want, so it didn’t matter.”

label: Quote
value: Janet said: "No, I guess not. I was afraid to try, anyway, for fear he’d think I meant it and just go. I suppose I’m a poor-spirited creature, but that is how I feel. And I can’t help it."

label: Quote
value: Janet said: “I dunno,” said Janet hopelessly. “I dunno if I could ever get up enough spunk. Things have drifted so long. But I’ll think it over.”

label: History
value: Lavendar Lewis lived at Echo Lodge
unit: Miss Lavendar Lewis lived at Echo Lodge alongside her young helper, Charlotta the Fourth. After Anne Shirley and Diana Barry accidentally discovered her home during a walk, Miss Lavendar hosted them for tea and heard mention of Paul Irving, the son of her former fiancé, Stephen Irving. Following a later visit where she recounted her past romance and quarrel with Stephen to Anne, Miss Lavendar met Paul and formed a fond friendship with him. Months later, Anne delivered a note to Miss Lavendar from Stephen, prompting a meeting at Echo Lodge where Miss Lavendar and Stephen reconciled. The pair were subsequently married in an intimate ceremony in her garden. In later years, Miss Lavendar hosted Anne during summer vacations, where Anne confided in her about refusing Gilbert Blythe's marriage proposal.

value: Lavendar Lewis said: "But oh, won’t you stay and have tea with me? Please, do. Mr. Kimball’s will have tea over before you get there. And Charlotta the Fourth and I will be so glad to have you."

label: Quote
value: Lavendar Lewis said: "to believe I’m old. Now, who are you . . . just for convenience’ sake? Diana Barry? And Anne Shirley? May I pretend that I’ve known you for a hundred years and call you Anne and Diana right away?"

label: Quote
value: Lavendar Lewis said: "I love them myself. They are very good company . . . with a little pretending. On calm evenings Charlotta the Fourth and I often sit out here and amuse ourselves with them. Charlotta, take back the horn and hang it carefully in its place."

label: Quote
value: Lavendar Lewis said: "It gave me a shock to hear about Stephen’s son that first day you were here, Anne. I’ve never been able to mention him to you since, but I’ve wanted to know all about him. What sort of a boy is he?"

label: Quote
value: Lavendar Lewis said: "Oh, I’m not so old as I thought . . . and I don’t need a single blue pill! Girls, when you come back with your strawberries we’ll have tea out here under the silver poplar. I’ll have it all ready for you with home-grown cream."

value: Leslie Moore is a clever woman.
unit: Leslie Moore is a clever, resolute woman who possesses a glowing, pent-up personality and a strong sense of duty. Though she is unhappy, a great change has come over her lately and she has been seen laughing and joking like a girl. She dislikes being pitied, is protective of taking her husband Dick around strangers, and once longed deeply to be a mother. A skilled dancer, she is also capable of exquisite embroidery and handwork. Looking to the future, she desires to make money to shingle her roof and intends to travel to Montreal in the fall to study nursing.

label: History
value: Leslie Moore is the daughter of Frank West
unit: Leslie Moore is the daughter of Frank West and Rose Elliott. She suffered early tragedy when her younger brother Kenneth died in a farm accident at age twelve, and two years later she discovered her father after he committed suicide. Raised by her mother, Leslie was coerced at age sixteen into marrying Dick Moore to prevent mortgage foreclosure on her family home. She subsequently lost her mother to pneumonia, but later used money inherited from her grandmother to complete two years of study in one year at Queen's Academy and briefly teach at the Glen school. Living a bitter, troubled life caring for her invalid husband, Leslie forms a friendship with her neighbor Anne Blythe after meeting her on the shore. Though initially envious of Anne's happy marriage, Leslie reconciles with her, and later forms a close connection with visiting author Owen Ford. She tearfully confesses her love for Owen to Anne after his departure, yet feels brokenhearted due to her marital situation. When Gilbert Blythe reveals a potential surgical treatment for her husband, Leslie chooses to finance the operation in Montreal; there, it is discovered that the man was actually Dick's cousin George, and that Dick had died years prior. Free from her burden, Leslie returns home and is eventually reunited with Owen, who declares his love for her in the Blythes' garden. The couple gets engaged, with Owen planning to purchase Anne and Gilbert's beloved house as a summer home.

label: Quote
value: Leslie Moore said: “I ENVY Anne,” said Leslie suddenly and fiercely, “and I’d envy her even if she had died! She was a mother for one beautiful day. I’d gladly give my life for THAT!”

label: Quote
value: Leslie Moore said: "If I had known I would have gone away—I wouldn’t have stayed here to meet him. You should have told me. It wasn’t fair of you, Anne—oh, it wasn’t fair!"

label: Quote
value: Leslie Moore said: "Anne likes the pink ones best, and Gilbert likes the white. But I want the crimson ones. They satisfy some craving in me as no other flower does."

label: Quote
value: Leslie Moore said: "It seems too great to be real—I’m afraid to speak of it—to think of it. It seems to me that it must just be another dream of this house of dreams and it will vanish when I leave here."

label: Quote
value: Leslie Moore said: "And, oh! I have such good news. He writes me that he is going to buy this place from the church trustees and keep it to spend our summer vacations in. Anne, are you not glad?"

label: Personality
value: Marilla Cuthbert is a self-contained woman.
unit: A self-contained, sensible woman of narrow experience, she possesses a rigid conscience and a strict devotion to what she perceives as her duty. Characterized as practical, non-imaginative, and stern, she values neatness and order, detests cats, and firmly disapproves of displaying deep emotion. Despite her unsympathetic and often sarcastic demeanor—particularly when suffering from headaches or after a moment of self-betrayal—she is known to have mellowed over time. She refuses on principle to criticize ministers in any form, proves cautious and deliberate when making decisions, and is noted for her skill in making braided mats and celebrated homemade currant wine. When raising a child, she favors moral lessons and inexorable discipline, conceiving it her duty to instill a tranquil uniformity of disposition. Deep down, nothing in her life brings her greater happiness than knowing Anne Shirley is going to marry Gilbert Blythe.

unit: Marilla Cuthbert lived at Green Gables for sixty years, having grown up in the home built during her youth alongside her brother Matthew. In her childhood, she heard an aunt call her a dark, homely little thing and was raised under traditional discipline rules where children were expected to keep still. When Matthew brought orphan Anne Shirley to Green Gables by mistake, Marilla was initially shocked and intended to return her, but she reconsidered upon learning of Anne's past hardships and seeing her distress at the prospect of living with Mrs. Blewett. Marilla resolved to raise Anne properly and educated her, although she often found herself exasperated by Anne's imaginative theatricality, such as when Anne dyed her hair green and Marilla had to cut it off. During a long recovery after Anne broke her ankle, Marilla realized how deeply she cared for the girl. As time passed, Marilla agreed to let Anne join Miss Stacy's advanced class, supported her through Queen's Academy, and mourned deeply alongside her when Matthew died suddenly of a heart attack. Confronted with the prospect of total blindness, Marilla was spared selling Green Gables when Anne chose to forgo her college scholarship to stay home and care for her. To ease their household management and allow Anne to attend college later, Marilla invited the widowed Rachel Lynde to move into Green Gables and took in two orphaned distant relatives, Davy and Dora Keith. She eventually saw Anne marry Gilbert Blythe at Green Gables, attended their first Christmas dinner at Four Winds, and stayed by Anne's side to offer support when Anne gave birth to her first child.

label: Quote
value: Marilla Cuthbert said: “There, there, Marilla, you can have your own way,” said Matthew reassuringly. “Only be as good and kind to her as you can without spoiling her. I kind of think she’s one of the sort you can do anything with if you only get her to love you.”

label: Quote
value: Marilla Cuthbert said: "Matthew Cuthbert, I’m astonished at you. You know that Anne’s behavior was dreadful, and yet you take her part! I suppose you’ll be saying next thing that she oughtn’t to be punished at all!"

label: Quote
value: Marilla Cuthbert said: "She’ll have her meals regular, and I’ll carry them up to her myself. But she’ll stay up there until she’s willing to apologize to Mrs. Lynde, and that’s final, Matthew."

label: Quote
value: Marilla Cuthbert said: "and I can’t prevent her, for her father aids and abets her. She’s always poring over a book. I’m glad she has the prospect of a playmate—perhaps it will take her more out-of-doors."

label: Quote
value: Marilla Cuthbert said: “I’ll go and have another look,” said Marilla, determining to be just. “If you put that brooch back it’s there still. If it isn’t I’ll know you didn’t, that’s all!”

label: History
value: Marshall Elliott was a noted dancer in his youth.
unit: Marshall Elliott was a noted dancer in his youth who vowed to never shave his face or cut his hair until the Liberals won political power. Over the years, he frequented the Four Winds lighthouse, where he celebrated New Year's Eve with Captain Jim, Anne, Gilbert, and Leslie, dancing around the fire with Leslie. Following a general election that resulted in a Liberal victory, Marshall finally shaved his long-kept beard and cut his hair.

label: Personality
value: Matthew Cuthbert is an exceptionally quiet man.
unit: Matthew Cuthbert is an exceptionally quiet, shy, and good-natured man who avoids excitement and rarely volunteers information or engages in arguments. Despite his intense shyness around strangers and a deep-seated dread of women and little girls, whom he fears are secretly laughing at him, he is a deeply sympathetic and indulgent listener. He is known for his patient and persistent nature, quietly holding fast to his opinions once formed. Though noted for being unobservant and hardworking, he possesses a wise and kind demeanor that earns admiration. He famously wished to keep Anne Shirley, offering her a loving and supportive presence.

value: Matthew Cuthbert was an extremely shy man.
unit: Matthew Cuthbert was an extremely shy man who dreaded almost all women except his sister Marilla and Mrs. Rachel Lynde. Due to his quiet nature, he rarely left home, and local boys found it difficult to get acquainted with him. When Matthew went to Bright River station to pick up an orphan boy to help on the farm, he was surprised to find a talkative young girl named Anne instead. Although Marilla initially intended to send Anne back, Matthew gently advocated for keeping her. As Anne settled into Green Gables, Matthew showed her quiet kindness, bringing her sweeties and offering warm encouragement for her schoolwork. Observing that Anne lacked stylish clothing like her peers, he sought the help of Mrs. Lynde to secure a brown dress with puffed sleeves for her as a Christmas gift. Over the years, he took immense pride in Anne's academic achievements, including her entrance into Queen's Academy and her winning of the Avery Scholarship. Following Anne's return home, Matthew's health began to fail. Shortly thereafter, he suffered a fatal collapse after reading news of a bank failure, leaving Marilla and Anne to mourn his loss.

label: History
value: Owen Ford is a newspaper writer
unit: A newspaper writer who previously published magazine short stories, Owen Ford suffered a severe case of typhoid fever and traveled to the sea to recuperate. While boarding in the area, he met Captain Jim, who shared his treasured life-book and stories with Owen, inspiring Owen to spend the summer writing a novel based on the old man's life. During his stay, Owen fell deeply in love with Leslie Moore, though he initially felt forced to leave her without expressing his feelings due to her difficult circumstances. Upon returning to Four Winds for a later visit, Owen declared his love to Leslie in the garden and was overjoyed when she confessed her love for him in return.

label: Quote
value: Owen Ford said: "Mrs. Blythe, this is a wonderful book—absolutely wonderful. If I could take it and use the material for a book I feel certain I could make the novel of the year out of it. Do you suppose Captain Jim would let me do it?"

label: Quote
value: Owen Ford said: "You will give the soul and I the body. Oh, we’ll write a famous book between us, Captain Jim. And we’ll get right to work."

label: Quote
value: Owen Ford said: "but in the main it’s done. I wrote the last sentence this morning. If I can find a publisher for it it will probably be out next summer or fall."

label: Quote
value: Owen Ford said: "Yes—love triumphant and perfect. Leslie, you know—you understand. I have loved you from the first. And I KNOW you love me—I don’t need to ask you. But I want to hear you say it—my darling—my darling!"

label: Quote
value: Owen Ford said: "But he must often be lonely. There was a touch of the seer about him tonight—he spoke as one to whom it had been given to speak. Well, I must be going, too."

label: History
value: Paul Irving is an imaginative student
unit: Paul Irving, an imaginative student who lost his mother three years prior, cheered his new teacher, Anne, on her first day of school by gifting her wild orchids. He shared a close bond with Anne, often writing about and discussing his rich inner world, including imaginary shore friends, rock people, and childhood worries. Deeply distressed upon learning that Anne was resigning from her teaching post to attend college, he accompanied her to Echo Lodge, where he bonded with Miss Lavendar over their shared experiences with imaginary dream-people. After meeting his returning father, Stephen Irving, Paul became excited to move to Boston following his father's wedding to Miss Lavendar. Years later, Paul returned as a guest to Green Gables to celebrate Anne's wedding to Gilbert Blythe.

value: Paul Irving said: “Yes; but if dryads are foolish they must take the consequences, just as if they were real people,” said Paul gravely. “Do you know what I think about the new moon, teacher? I think it is a little golden boat full of dreams.”

label: Quote
value: Paul Irving said: "I’ve eaten enough to make anyone grow. I do hope, now that I’ve begun, I’ll keep on till I’m as tall as father. He is six feet, you know, Miss Lavendar."

label: Quote
value: Paul Irving said: "I think you would make a splendid mother. You have just the right look in your eyes . . . the look my little mother always had. I think it’s a pity you haven’t any boys of your own."

value: Paul Irving said: "you can’t think what has happened! Something so splendid. Father is here . . . just think of that! Father is here! Come right in. Father, this is my beautiful teacher. You know, father."

label: History
value: Philippa Gordon is the daughter of a prominent man from a Bluenose family in Bolingbroke, Nova Scotia.
unit: Philippa Gordon, the daughter of a prominent man from a Bluenose family in Bolingbroke, Nova Scotia, first met Anne Shirley and Priscilla Grant while exploring Old St. John's Cemetery near Redmond College. She quickly adopted them into her social circle and eventually persuaded them to let her join their household at Patty's Place. While spending a summer at a boardinghouse, Phil met a divinity student named Jonas Blake, whose sermon deeply moved her and inspired feelings of love. She later accepted Jonas's marriage proposal and shared the news with Anne. After graduating from Redmond College, Phil comforted Anne when Anne rejected Royal Gardner's marriage proposal. Phil subsequently married Jonas, with Anne serving as her bridesmaid. Years later, Phil returned to Green Gables as a guest to attend Anne and Gilbert's wedding.

value: Phil Gordon said: "I’ll go, if I can walk with Priscilla and Charlie. That will be a bearable degree of gooseberry. That Gilbert of yours is a darling, Anne, but why does he go around so much with Goggle-eyes?"

label: Quote
value: Phil Gordon said: "I don’t want William’s Island especially, but I’m sure I couldn’t get it if I did. Look at that sentry on the summit of the fort, right beside the flag. Doesn’t he look as if he had stepped out of a romance?"

label: Quote
value: Phil Gordon said: "Look—in white letters, around the archway over the gate. ‘Patty’s Place.’ Isn’t that killing? Especially on this Avenue of Pinehursts and Elmwolds and Cedarcrofts? ‘Patty’s Place,’ if you please! I adore it."

label: Quote
value: Phil Gordon said: "Joseph, you calico beastie, don’t you dare jump on my lap. I won’t go to a dance all over cat hairs. No, Anne, I won’t look matronly. But no doubt I’ll be married."

label: Quote
value: Phil Gordon said: "No, he would do if he wasn’t poor. I must marry a rich man, Aunt Jamesina. That—and good looks—is an indispensable qualification. I’d marry Gilbert Blythe if he were rich."

label: History
value: Priscilla Grant attended Queen's school
unit: Priscilla Grant attended Queen's school with Anne Shirley and was the niece of author Mrs. Charlotte E. Morgan. During a spring picnic walk in Avonlea with her friends, she poetically imagined nature alongside Anne while exploring the hidden garden of Hester Gray. She later surprised Anne with an unexpected visit to Green Gables, bringing her aunt Mrs. Morgan along for dinner. Priscilla went on to study at Redmond College, greeting Anne upon her arrival in Kingsport and helping her settle into college life. She helped establish a shared household at Patty's Place with Anne, Stella Maynard, and Philippa Gordon, living there together throughout their remaining years at Redmond. She eventually married a handsome foreign missionary.

label: History
value: Mrs. Rachel Lynde was brought up with ten children
unit: Mrs. Rachel Lynde was brought up with ten children, losing two over the years, and married at eighteen after attending school with a red-haired girl. A long-standing resident of Avonlea who knitted sixteen cotton warp quilts, she lived alongside Marilla Cuthbert as a neighbor for forty-five years without a single quarrel. When Marilla's brother Matthew set out to adopt an orphan boy, Rachel visited Green Gables to investigate and warned Marilla against taking in an unknown child. She later met the adopted girl, Anne, but offended her with blunt comments about her red hair, prompting an explosive outburst that ended only after Anne dramatically apologized to win Rachel's forgiveness and friendship. Over the years, Rachel often advised Marilla on raising Anne, including letting the girl stay home from school after a harsh punishment, and she even stepped in to sew Anne a stylish brown dress with puffed sleeves for Christmas when Matthew struggled to shop for it. She celebrated Anne's academic triumphs and offered comfort when Matthew passed away suddenly, while continuously tracking local town developments. Following the death of her own husband, Thomas Lynde, Rachel accepted Marilla's invitation to move into Green Gables so she could remain in Avonlea, which cleared the way for Anne to leave her teaching post for college. Living at Green Gables, Rachel helped care for the twins, Davy and Dora, while managing household affairs alongside Marilla. She welcomed Anne home during college breaks, remained a staple of community news and wedding preparations, and eventually attended Anne and Gilbert Blythe's marriage ceremony before traveling to Four Winds to share Christmas dinner at their new home.

label: Quote
value: Roy Gardner said: "That ought to be sufficient introduction. My name is Royal Gardner. And you are the Miss Shirley who read the Tennyson paper at the Philomathic the other evening, aren’t you?"

label: Quote
value: Roy Gardner said: "I feel as if I didn’t belong anywhere yet. I put in my Freshman and Sophomore years at Redmond two years ago. I’ve been in Europe ever since. Now I’ve come back to finish my Arts course."

label: Quote
value: Roy Gardner said: "I can’t understand it—I can’t believe you are not the woman I’ve believed you to be. But reproaches are idle between us. You are the only woman I can ever love. I thank you for your friendship, at least. Good-bye, Anne."

label: History
value: Ruby Gillis grew up with many big sisters.
unit: Ruby Gillis grew up with many big sisters and once used a magic pebble to charm away her warts. During her school days, she formed a Story Club alongside Anne and Jane Andrews. Ruby expressed a childhood wish to have dozens of beaus when she grew up, and she visited Boston the fall before falling ill. During Anne's time at Redmond, Ruby sent updates from home in a bundle of letters. After Anne returned to Avonlea, she learned that Ruby was terminally ill with consumption, even though Ruby stubbornly insisted she was healthy during a visit at her home. Later, Ruby tearfully confessed her fear of dying to Anne during an evening together, but she passed away peacefully in her sleep the following night.

unit: Ruby Gillis grew up with many big sisters and once used a magic pebble to charm away her warts. During her school days, she formed a Story Club alongside Anne and Jane Andrews. Ruby expressed a childhood wish to have dozens of beaus when she grew up, and she visited Boston the fall before falling ill. During Anne's time at Redmond, Ruby sent updates from home in a bundle of letters. After Anne returned to Avonlea, she learned that Ruby was terminally ill with consumption, even though Ruby stubbornly insisted she was healthy during a visit at her home. Later, Ruby tearfully confessed her fear of dying to Anne during an evening together, but she passed away peacefully in her sleep the following night.

label: Quote
value: Ruby Gillis said: "There’s a concert at Carmody and a party at White Sands. Herb Spencer’s going to take me. He’s my latest. Be sure to come up tomorrow. I’m dying for a good talk with you. I want to hear all about your doings at Redmond."

label: Quote
value: Ruby Gillis said: "Me! Why, I’m perfectly well. I never felt better in my life. Of course, that congestion last winter pulled me down a little. But just see my color. I don’t look much like an invalid, I’m sure."

label: Quote
value: Ruby Gillis said: "Anne, it won’t be long now before I’ll be lying over there. You and Diana and all the rest will be going about, full of life—and I’ll be there—in the old graveyard—dead!"

label: Quote
value: Ruby Gillis said: "I’ll try. I’ll think over what you have said, and try to believe it. And you’ll come up as often as you can, won’t you, Anne?"

label: Quote
value: Ruby Gillis said: “Nor I,” said Ruby Gillis, with a shiver. “I don’t mind floating down when there’s two or three of us in the flat and we can sit up. It’s fun then. But to lie down and pretend I was dead—I just couldn’t. I’d die really of fright.”

After Anne Shirley became trapped in the roof of the duckhouse while trying to look through a window, Sarah returned after a rainstorm and freed her. Sarah listened to Anne's explanation, shared tea with her, and sold her a blue willow-ware platter for twenty-five dollars.

label: History
value: Shirley pursued her education
unit: Shirley pursued her education and career, working as a teacher at Avonlea school before leaving to attend Redmond College after Rachel Lynde moved into Green Gables. During a summer vacation in Avonlea, she admitted to Miss Lavendar that she had refused Gilbert's proposal. Later, after being rescued in a downpour by Royal Gardner, a handsome student who sent her roses, Shirley wondered if she had found her ideal prince. However, upon returning to Green Gables from Echo Lodge and discovering that Gilbert was critically ill with typhoid fever, she endured a grief-stricken night and realized her true, deep love for him. After Gilbert recovered, the two planned their future, and friends and guests gathered at Green Gables ahead of their ceremony. On her wedding day, Shirley wed Gilbert in the orchard before departing with him for Glen St. Mary.

value: Shirley said: "Fare thee well, my beloved friend. Henceforth we must be as strangers though living side by side. But my heart will ever be faithful to thee."

label: Quote
value: Shirley said: "That is all there is left in life for me, now that my friend has been ruthlessly torn from me. In school I can look at her and muse over days departed."

value: Shirley said: “I think he has only been its nominal head for many years,” said Anne. “He is a very old man; his nephews are really at the head of the institution.”

label: Quote
value: Shirley said: “If I had been the boy you sent for,” said Anne wistfully, “I’d be able to help you so much now and spare you in a hundred ways. I could find it in my heart to wish I had been, just for that.”

label: Diana Barry
value: Diana is Anne's bosom friend
unit: Diana is Anne's bosom friend, though their close companionship faced an early trial when Mrs. Barry forced them apart and forbade Diana from playing with Anne. Despite this temporary separation, they maintained secret notes and rekindled their deep bond upon Anne's return to school and home. Over the years, they have shared major life milestones together, from exchanging confidences about Diana's engagement to Fred Wright to preparing for weddings and handling Anne's departures.

label: Quote
value: Stella Maynard said: "I love Anne and I like Roy. Everybody says she is making a brilliant match, and even Mrs. Gardner thinks her charming now. It all sounds as if it were made in heaven, but I have my doubts. Make the most of that, Aunt Jamesina."

label: Quote
value: Stella Maynard said: “Well, I don’t know how he and the Sarah-cat will ever make out to live together,” said Stella pesimistically. “Cat-fights in the orchard o’nights are bad enough. But cat-fights here in the livingroom are unthinkable.”

label: Quote
value: Stella Maynard said: "I was afraid they’d come back. And then our jolly little nest here would be broken up—and we poor callow nestlings thrown out on the cruel world of boardinghouses again."

label: Quote
value: Stella Maynard said: "Nothing seems worthwhile. My very thoughts are old. I’ve thought them all before. What is the use of living after all, Anne?"

label: Quote
value: Stella Maynard said: "Oh, my mind agrees with you, Anne. But my soul remains doleful and uninspired. I’m always grubby and dingy on rainy nights."

label: Quote
value: Susan said: “Do not tell me,” said Susan fiercely, answering the anguish in Marilla’s eyes, “that God could be so cruel as to take that darling lamb from us when we all love her so much.”

label: Quote
value: Susan said: “Now for breakfast,” she said briskly. “I am of the opinion that we will all be glad of a bite and sup. You tell young Mrs. Doctor not to worry about a single thing—Susan is at the helm. You tell her just to think of her baby.”

label: Quote
value: Susan said: "Oh, the poor lamb—the poor lamb! How can she bear it, Miss Cuthbert? I am afraid it will kill her. She has been that built up and happy, longing for that baby, and planning for it. Cannot anything be done nohow, Miss Cuthbert?"

label: Quote
value: Susan said: “And it is such a sweet baby,” sobbed Susan. “I never saw one so white—they are mostly red or yallow. And it opened its big eyes as if it was months old. The little, little thing! Oh, the poor, young Mrs. Doctor!”

label: Quote
value: Susan said: "Have a good time and do not worry about the pantry. Susan is at the helm. There is no use in keeping a dog and doing your own barking. I am going to take your breakfast up to you every morning."

label: History
value: Captain Jim ran off to sea as a young man.
unit: As a young man, Captain Jim ran off to sea, driven by his maternal seafaring heritage, and he spent many years sailing aboard the Gray Gull alongside his old crony Henry Pollack. Although he had no children of his own, he bore the enduring loss of his childhood sweetheart, Margaret, who had tragically drifted away at sea over fifty years prior. Decades after these early adventures, he welcomed Anne and Gilbert Blythe upon their arrival in Four Winds, quickly recognizing Anne as a kindred spirit and establishing a close friendship with the couple. He routinely entertained visitors at the Four Winds lighthouse with his collection of curiosities and extensive sea tales, while also remaining a steady pillar of the community by escorting Dick Moore home to Leslie and providing financial assistance through a mortgage so Dick could undergo surgery in Montreal. When Owen Ford visited the harbor, Captain Jim discovered that Owen was the grandson of his old schoolmaster’s bride; he subsequently lent Owen his personal life-book, which Owen adapted into a finished novel incorporating Margaret's memory. Later, Captain Jim gave his heartfelt benediction to Leslie and Owen after they confessed their mutual love, and he asked Anne to care for his cat, First Mate, as he contemplated his mortality. Shortly after receiving the very first printed copy of his published life story from Anne and Leslie, Captain Jim passed away peacefully overnight on his sofa while reading its final pages.

value: Uncle Jim said: “Oh, I do, Mistress Doctor, I do,” protested Captain Jim. “Why, I live like a king gen’rally. Last night I was up to the Glen and took home two pounds of steak. I meant to have a spanking good dinner today.”

label: Quote
value: Uncle Jim said: "The Government don’t give lighthouse keepers such luxuries. Look at the colors that wood makes. If you’d like some driftwood for your fire, Mistress Blythe, I’ll bring you up a load some day. Sit down. I’m going to make you a cup of tea."

label: Quote
value: Uncle Jim said: "That’s Marshall Elliott—a mighty fine man with jest one streak of foolishness in him. I s’pose you wondered what his object was in turning himself into a sort of dime museum freak."

label: Quote

chapter: v3 · Chapter XXI Roses of Yesterday
unit: During her stay in Bolingbroke with Phil Gordon, Anne visits her humble birthplace and meets the woman currently living there. The woman allows Anne to explore the house, including the room where she was born, and hands over a small packet of old letters written by Anne's parents. Anne later visits her parents' grave and reads the letters, feeling for the first time that she truly knows them.

label: v2 · II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure
value: Anne and Diana discuss Village Improvement Society plans.
chapter: v2 · II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure
unit: Anne and Diana discuss Village Improvement Society plans on their drive home from Carmody when they spot a Jersey cow trampling Mr. Harrison's oat field. Believing the cow is her own nuisance Jersey, Dolly, Anne impulsively sells the stray cow on the spot to Mr. Shearer for twenty dollars. Upon returning to Green Gables, Anne discovers Dolly still in the barnyard and realizes she accidentally sold Mr. Harrison's cow, prompting her to head over to his house with the money and a cake to confess.

unit: Anne and Priscilla settle into college life at Redmond as their freshman class wins the annual Arts Rush under Gilbert Blythe's leadership. label: v2 · II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure
value: Anne and Diana discuss Village Improvement Society plans.
chapter: v2 · II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure
unit: Anne and Diana discuss Village Improvement Society plans on their drive home from Carmody when they spot a Jersey cow trampling Mr. Harrison's oat field. Believing the cow is her own nuisance Jersey, Dolly, Anne impulsively sells the stray cow on the spot to Mr. Shearer for twenty dollars. Upon returning to Green Gables, Anne discovers Dolly still in the barnyard and realizes she accidentally sold Mr. Harrison's cow, prompting her to head over to his house with the money and a cake to confess.

unit: On the eve of the school term, Anne discusses teaching methods and classroom discipline with Jane and Gilbert, strongly opposing corporal punishment. After returning to Green Gables, she visits Mr. Harrison, who also doubts her plan to rule by affection rather than the rod. The next morning, a nervous Anne drinks ginger tea prepared by Marilla before starting her first day of teaching.

unit: Anne and Diana continue canvassing Avonlea for subscriptions, encountering peculiar neighbors like the hyper-neat Mrs. Theodore White and receiving mixed results. Gilbert Blythe rows by and rescues her, but Anne angrily refuses his offer of friendship. After returning home safely, Anne reflects on learning another lesson, while Matthew quietly encourages her not to abandon all her romance.

chapter: v2 · IV Different Opinions
unit: On the eve of the school term, Anne discusses teaching methods and classroom discipline with Jane and Gilbert, strongly opposing corporal punishment. After returning to Green Gables, she visits Mr. Harrison, who also doubts her plan to rule by affection rather than the rod. The next morning, a nervous Anne drinks ginger tea prepared by Marilla before starting her first day of teaching.

chapter: v2 · VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women
unit: Anne and Diana continue canvassing Avonlea for subscriptions, encountering peculiar neighbors like the hyper-neat Mrs. Theodore White and receiving mixed results. Learning that Lorenzo White just had a new baby boy, Anne strategically visits him while he is overjoyed, securing a generous five-dollar donation. Later that evening, Anne visits Mr. Harrison to ask for a contribution, but he flatly refuses.

unit: In a bad mood from a toothache, Anne accidentally causes fireworks to explode in the schoolroom and subsequently whips Anthony Pye after he puts a mouse in her desk. She goes home heartbroken over her bad day, but Marilla comforts her. The next morning, Anthony treats Anne with new respect, and Mrs. Rachel Lynde later confirms that the whipping gained his approval.

chapter: v3 · Chapter V Letters from Home
unit: Anne and Priscilla settle into college life at Redmond as their freshman class wins the annual Arts Rush under Gilbert Blythe's leadership. Philippa Gordon quickly adopts Anne and Priscilla, introducing them into Redmond's active social circle. Anne receives a bundle of letters from home—including updates from Jane, Ruby, Diana, Marilla, Mrs. Lynde, and Davy—which helps connect her old life in Avonlea to her new life in Kingsport.

value: Anne and Diana discuss Village Improvement Society plans.
chapter: v2 · II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure
unit: Anne and Diana discuss Village Improvement Society plans on their drive home from Carmody when they spot a Jersey cow trampling Mr. Harrison's oat field. Believing the cow is her own nuisance Jersey, Dolly, Anne impulsively sells the stray cow on the spot to Mr. Shearer for twenty dollars. Upon returning to Green Gables, Anne discovers Dolly still in the barnyard and realizes she accidentally sold Mr. Harrison's cow, prompting her to head over to his house with the money and a cake to confess.

chapter: v2 · IV Different Opinions
unit: On the eve of the school term, Anne discusses teaching methods and classroom discipline with Jane and Gilbert, strongly opposing corporal punishment. After returning to Green Gables, she visits Mr. Harrison, who also doubts her plan to rule by affection rather than the rod. The next morning, a nervous Anne drinks ginger tea prepared by Marilla before starting her first day of teaching.

chapter: v3 · Chapter V Letters from Home
unit: Anne and Priscilla settle into college life at Redmond as their freshman class wins the annual Arts Rush under Gilbert Blythe's leadership. Anne receives a bundle of letters from home—including updates from Jane, Ruby, Diana, Marilla, Mrs. Lynde, and Davy—which helps connect her old life in Avonlea to her new life in Kingsport.

unit: Anne and Diana continue canvassing Avonlea for subscriptions, encountering peculiar neighbors like the hyper-neat Mrs. Theodore White and receiving mixed results. unit: Anne and her friends re-enact a poem on a flat-bottomed boat, but the boat begins to leak, stranding Anne on a bridge pile. After returning home safely, Anne reflects on learning another lesson, while Matthew quietly encourages her not to abandon all her romance.

chapter: v2 · II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure
unit: Anne and Diana discuss Village Improvement Society plans on their drive home from Carmody when they spot a Jersey cow trampling Mr. Harrison's oat field. Believing the cow is her own nuisance Jersey, Dolly, Anne impulsively sells the stray cow on the spot to Mr. Shearer for twenty dollars. Upon returning to Green Gables, Anne discovers Dolly still in the barnyard and realizes she accidentally sold Mr. Harrison's cow, prompting her to head over to his house with the money and a cake to confess.

Returning home, Anne discusses her day with Marilla Cuthbert and Mrs. Rachel Lynde.

The next morning, Anthony treats Anne with new respect, and Mrs. Rachel Lynde later confirms that the whipping gained his approval.

value: Marilla returns home to Green Gables.
chapter: CHAPTER XXVII. Vanity and Vexation of Spirit
unit: Marilla returns home to Green Gables expecting supper, but finds the stove unlit and Anne nowhere in sight. When Marilla goes upstairs, she discovers Anne hiding under her pillows because she dyed her red hair green using hair dye bought from a peddler. After washing fails to remove the green color, Marilla cuts Anne's hair off short, leaving Anne to reflect remorsefully on her vanity.

Anne decides to forfeit her college scholarship, stay at home to care for Marilla, and take up a local teaching job instead. After learning Gilbert Blythe gave up the Avonlea school so she could have it, Anne meets Gilbert on her way home and they finally end their feud to become close friends.

unit: Anne and Diana continue canvassing Avonlea for subscriptions, encountering peculiar neighbors like the hyper-neat Mrs. Theodore White and receiving mixed results. section: Chapter XXXII Tea with Mrs. Douglas
label: Chapter XXXII Tea with Mrs. Douglas
value: Anne accompanies Janet to a prayer meeting.
chapter: Chapter XXXII Tea with Mrs. Douglas
unit: Anne accompanies Janet to a prayer meeting in Valley Road, where she meets John Douglas, Janet's quiet admirer.
